newsitem.title: UK: Go-Ahead says no clash on trains and buses.
newsitem.headline: Go-Ahead says no clash on trains and buses.

text.p: British bus company Go-Ahead Plc said on Thursday it stood by its assesment that its interest in rail firm Victory Rail, which operates Thames Trains, did not conflict with its existing bus businesses in the same area.
Earlier Britain's Office of Fair Trading said it would seek comments from interested parties on the competition effects of Victory's operations as the first stage of a possible review.

Go-Ahead managing director Martin Ballinger told Reuters that, "prior to sanctioning the Thames Trains franchise bid the Go-Ahead board had taken leading counsel advice and consulted a wide range of parties."
"The board believes it is unlikely that the supportive comments made at that time are likely to be changed in the face of this OFT procedure".
Although Go-Ahead operates buses in the city of Oxford and between Oxford and London, Ballinger said the inter-city buses used "a totally different route from that taken by the train".

He added that the firm was a minority operator on this coach route where it has a bigger rival in the market. It had observed last year, when the two made various price and service changes in competition, that there had been a negligible effect on the rail market, he added.
